title: Everyone's learning to prompt better. That's the wrong skill.
why_read: A contrarian take arguing prompt engineering is overrated and pointing toward a different underlying skill, likely to prompt some genuine reflection for engineers investing heavily in prompting techniques.
analysis: The author argues that the current obsession with learning prompting techniques is misdirected effort, since it doesn't address the deeper problem that determines whether AI-assisted work actually succeeds. Although the excerpt cuts off before revealing what the 'one skill that matters' actually is, the framing (that better prompts can't fix certain fundamental risks) is a reasonable critique of prompt-engineering hype. It's a personal essay rather than a technical deep dive, so its value is more in reframing thinking than in offering concrete techniques.
